The handle survives a reload and signing in from another browser. A comment and the presence tooltip show the same handle. Limits A handle is not a login: you still sign in with your email. A handle can change, but comment history is not rewritten: an old comment keeps the handle it had when sent. A taken handle is refused with HANDLE_TAKEN .

en.title: Task budget and limits
en.summary: Two limits are set in the dialog — changes and money; tokens and time are server defaults. A task without a budget is not created.
en.text: Result You set the limits before the run, and the agent cannot exceed them. When a limit is reached the task fails without a partial write. What is limited Changes — how many objects the agent may create. This is the "Max changes" field in the dialog; it is checked before writing. Money — the maximum cost in dollars at the provider's price. This is the "Max cost, $" field; it is checked after the model call. Tokens — how much the model may read and write. The dialog does not set them: the server uses 8 000 tokens unless the request says otherwise. Time — how many seconds the task may run. The dialog does not set it: the server uses 120 seconds unless the request says otherwise. The rule A task without a budget is not created. That is not paperwork: the budget is your consent to spend money and change the room. The server fills in the token and time defaults only once a budget exists. Steps In the agent dialog set "Max changes". Set "Max cost, $". Run the task. If it did not work "Set a limit". The changes field is empty or zero; the task was not created. BUDGET_EXCEEDED or BUDGET_ACTIONS . The agent stopped; a partial result is not applied. Raise the limit and run again. TOO_MANY_TASKS . This room has reached its task limit. Wait for a task to finish or cancel one.

en.title: Model call journal
en.summary: What is recorded about each call, how to verify the chain, and what a break means.
en.text: Result An organisation administrator sees which model calls happened, with what parameters and cost, and can verify that the record was not altered. What is recorded Provider, model, skill and skill version. Tokens, cost, latency and error code. The key fingerprint, never the key itself. A record hash linked to the previous one: the journal is a chain. The prompt text and room content are not in the journal. Steps Open Organisation → Agents → Evidential journal . Filter by skill or outcome. Click "Verify chain". What the check means "Chain verified". Every record is present and matches its hash. "Chain broken at #N". A record was changed or removed; that is a fact about the journal, not a rendering glitch. Tell the administrator. Limits Only the Organisation admin and Security admin roles see the journal; everyone else gets a refusal. The check is an explicit action: it recomputes hashes and never runs in the background.

en.title: Room agent
en.summary: Fifteen scenarios: process, sprint, requirements, MVP, retrospective, decision, meeting actions, prioritisation, competitors, architecture, ideas, dependencies, user flow, system architecture and problem map.
en.text: What it is The room owner assigns one active agent to the room. The agent writes a first draft from your request straight into the room, and the team continues with the usual tools: editing objects, commenting and deleting what is not needed. Fifteen scenarios: a process map , a sprint or phase plan , requirements , MVP , a retrospective , a decision , meeting actions , prioritisation , competitors , an architecture decision , ideas , dependencies , a user flow , a system architecture and a problem map from interviews. Who can ask The room owner assigns their own active agent, turns it on and gives it tasks. Selected editors can give tasks. The owner selects them under Who can give tasks in the agent panel. Clearing the checkbox stops that editor’s unfinished tasks. Other organisation members with access to the room read the task history, open drafts and edit them according to their role. A guest works with objects according to their role but does not see the task history. A public-link visitor cannot run the agent: while the link is on, assignment and new tasks are closed. Before you start Agents are enabled in the organisation: Organisation → Agents. The owner has created an agent and assigned it to the room from the avatar in the header. A provider key is configured for a real draft. Without a key the task stays queued and runs once the key appears. Steps Select the notes or cards the request is about. The selection is the agent's source. Press the agent avatar in the header. Write the request and choose a kind: Process map, Sprint or phase, Requirements, MVP, Retrospective, Decision, Meeting actions, Prioritisation, Competitors, Architecture decision, Ideas, Dependencies, User flow, Architecture or Problem map. Check how many sources will be sent and press Create draft. Wait for Draft ready. An ordinary editable frame appears in the room; Show on canvas moves the camera to it. Discuss and edit it like any other objects. A refinement in the same thread creates a new frame beside the previous one; the previous version keeps all manual edits. Undo The server writes the draft, so it is not in the ordinary ⌘Z history. If you gave the task in this tab, ⌘Z after the draft appears removes it as a whole when no newer local edit stands in front of it. If there were edits, they are undone first, then the draft. The panel has the same Undo draft button. If an older draft sits outside its frame, Fit frame expands the frame to its objects. History The room owner can delete one conversation or the whole agent history. Frames stay ordinary room objects, and an unfinished task in a deleted conversation is stopped. History deletion is not undone by ⌘Z; the deletion itself is recorded in the audit. Public link and ownership To enable a public link, turn off the agent and confirm that visitors can see existing drafts. Task history is available to organisation members with room access. When the room changes owner, the assignment is cleared, unfinished tasks stop, and the history and already written frames remain. Limits One agent per room and one running task; further requests wait in the queue. A draft is new objects inside a new frame. Existing objects are not changed. The agent sees only explicitly selected material, the request text and the messages of this thread. A selected frame expands to the objects inside it; when the frame is a table, the agent sees its axes and each object's cell. Comments are not part of the context.

en.title: Ask an agent to change the room
en.summary: Four scenarios — a plan with a preview, a diagram straight onto the room, cards as a package and tidying into columns; what goes to the model and what happens without a key.
en.text: Result An agent does a task in the room on your behalf. There are four scenarios, and they change the room differently: Plan (the Brief to room skill): the agent proposes a structure, you read the preview and press Apply. The room does not change before that, and one ⌘Z removes the whole structure. Diagram (the Diagram from a description skill): the agent writes shapes and connectors immediately, with no preview; ⌘Z does not undo that write. Cards (the Cards from a selection skill): the agent builds a package from the selection. Preview job shows the card count, Run job creates them; ⌘Z does not undo the package. Tidy up (the Tidy up selection skill): the agent lays the selection out in even columns. You choose the layout in the before/after preview and press Apply; one ⌘Z puts every object back. Who can ask An account with edit rights. The Ask AI… item in the More ▾ menu is shown only to someone who can change the room: an editor, a co-owner or the owner. A public-link visitor gets no AI entry: a link is a view grant, and an agent needs an account to act for. Even when you are signed in, if the only access to this room is the link, AI stays closed. A viewer or commenter can watch the room but cannot ask an agent: edit rights come first. Before you start Agents are enabled in the organisation and in the room. In the organisation an administrator enables them (Organisation → Agents); in the room the owner or a co-owner does. You have an active agent that you created: the list shows only your enabled agents, and nobody can run somebody else's agent. A plan or a diagram needs a provider key. Without a key the task does not fail with AI_NOT_CONFIGURED : it stays queued and runs once the key is configured. Cards do not call a model, and tidying works without a key. For cards and tidying, select the objects first: without a selection these skills are not offered. The brief file is optional. If you attach one, it must be .md , .txt or .csv in UTF-8, at most 100 000 bytes. Provider key A key is access to the provider budget. Create a separate key for remo with a spending cap and an expiry date; do not use your main personal key or share it. In remo the secret is stored encrypted in the database, shown once and decrypted only while a task runs; you can revoke it at any time. How a plan works Task. You describe the result and attach a file when you need one. Preview. The agent returns a plan: how many objects and connectors will appear, where they will sit, and what looks doubtful. The room does not change at this point. Apply. You read the plan and press Apply. All objects and connectors are written in one gesture. Undo. One ⌘Z removes the whole plan: objects and connectors alike. Opening it again. The plan shows the result and a "Show in room" button instead of Apply. If the same plan was open in two tabs, the tab that applies it second gets the server's "already applied" answer and writes nothing; it shows no ⌘Z hint, because it wrote nothing. Steps Open More ▾ and choose Ask AI… Choose an agent and a skill. Brief to room is selected by default; the list shows only skills compatible with the task and the selection, plus Auto. Auto picks a skill from the wording of the task. Check the source: the Source block shows how many objects and characters of the selection will reach the model. Remove keeps the task without object text; Selection only makes the selection the task itself. Describe the task: what should exist afterwards. Brief to room also accepts a .md , .txt or .csv file in UTF-8. Check "What will go to the model" and set a budget. The dialog sets changes and money; tokens and time are server defaults. Money may be fractional: 0.1 is ten cents, 0.25 a quarter. Click "Ask the agent" and wait for the plan ready status. The plan appears in the room as dashed lines, with a task panel at the bottom: the object count, the bounds and the buttons. Objects grouped by kind and warnings with their codes are under Details. Read the plan and press Apply. Reject closes the task and writes nothing. Esc hides the panel but does not reject the plan. After applying, the panel shows "⌘Z undoes the plan" and "Show in room". Diagram: straight onto the room Choose the Diagram from a description skill and describe the process. Click "Ask the agent" and wait for the applied status. Result: shapes and connectors appear in the current view. There is no preview, so the future diagram cannot be checked beforehand. One ⌘Z does not undo the diagram: delete the extra objects by hand or ask for a fresh diagram. A provider key is needed, as for a plan. Cards: a package Select the objects to turn into cards in the room: up to 500. Choose the Cards from a selection skill, where the cards should go, and what to do with the source — Keep or Move. Click "Preview job". Result: the card count; nothing is written to the room yet. Click "Run job". Result: cards appear in chunks, and the Card jobs list shows progress. A package can be stopped with Stop and resumed with Resume: progress is kept between chunks. This applies to a card package, not to a plan or diagram task. One ⌘Z does not undo the cards. Tidy up: columns Select sticky notes in the room. Press Tidy up in the context menu or on the selection bar. Choose a layout: Auto, By prefix, By type, Grid or By meaning. Natural order puts US-2 before US-10 . Wait for the preview: dashed lines in the room show where objects move and where blocks appear, and warnings name locked objects and foreign frames that stay put. Change the layout under Details if needed: block labels are kept and coordinates are recomputed. Press Apply. Sizes, texts and lines do not change; one ⌘Z puts everything back. If a frame is selected, its contents are laid out inside it and the frame itself does not move. Blocks are frames, never groups. The 50-object limit is counted after groups and the selected frame are expanded: a larger set is refused before a plan is stored. A kanban card stays in place with a warning: its cell decides where it stands, and the plan applies to the remaining objects. Check the result Plan. The object and connector counts in the preview match what appeared in the room. One ⌘Z returns the room to the state before the apply. Applying selects the created frames; "Show in room" only closes the preview and selects nothing. Tasks. In the agent dialog, "Recent tasks" shows the status and the task text; the created objects are visible in the room. Who sees the journals. The History tab in the organisation and the Evidential journal in Organisation → Agents are visible only to the Organisation admin and Security admin roles. An editor sees Recent tasks and the objects in the room, not those tabs. Audit and events. Applying a plan leaves organisation journal rows ("Plan approved", "Plan applied") but no board.item.created event. A card package creates objects through server commands, so each card produces a board.item.created event for webhooks. Diagram. Shapes and connectors appear in the current view; "Recent tasks" shows the applied status; the object info names the agent and the diagram skill. ⌘Z does not remove the diagram. Cards. The card count matches "Preview job"; the card job shows the applied status; the card info names the agent and the cards skill. Files and limits Brief formats: .md , .txt , .csv ; UTF-8 only. The file is optional. A file is at most 100 000 bytes; the model sees the first 20 000 characters of the extracted text, cut at a line boundary. The plan itself is never truncated. One plan carries up to 10 operations, 300 objects and 100 connectors; up to 12 columns, 50 stories per column, 6 swimlanes of 4 rows each. Above 200 objects the preview warns that the plan is close to the ceiling. Above 10 operations the reply is refused with TOO_MANY_OPERATIONS ; above 300 objects or placements, with PLAN_TOO_LARGE . In both cases the plan is not stored. Plan coordinates stay within ±1 000 000. Object text is at most 2 000 characters, a title 200. The room snapshot describes up to 200 objects. The selection text for a task is at most 50 objects and 20 000 characters; the cut is recorded on the task. A task without a budget is not created. The dialog sets changes and money; tokens (8 000) and time (120 seconds) are server defaults unless the request sets them explicitly. A card package holds up to 500 objects, in chunks of 50. Tidying takes up to 50 objects and 20 000 characters of selection text; the limit is counted after groups and a selected frame are expanded. A larger set is refused before a plan is stored. What goes to the model The wording of the task. For a brief, the attached file as plain text; CSV rows become Header: value | Header: value . Long text is cut after 20 000 characters. A room snapshot of up to 200 objects: object, frame and kanban column ids, types, coordinates, sizes, parents and connector ends. Titles, sticky note text, comments and people are not sent. For a diagram, up to 20 short fragments of the selected objects, 200 characters each. For cards, no model is called. The task, the file and the room are data, not instructions. The model cannot change or delete existing objects, read another room or follow a link. If it did not work No Ask AI… item. You are a viewer, a commenter, a link visitor, or not signed in. "Set a limit". A task without a budget is not created. "Agents are off". An organisation administrator or the room owner (co-owner) turned them off. "The agent service is unreachable". Sync is not running; start it and click Retry. "You have no agents yet". Open Organisation → Agents → Create agent , enable it, then return to the room. The list shows only active agents you created. AGENT_DENIED . The task did not run: the agent is disabled, you no longer have access to the room, agents are off in the organisation or in the room, or the agent lacks write capabilities. The exact reason is next to the task in "Recent tasks". No key. The task does not fail: it stays queued and runs once the key is configured. Until then no plan preview appears. "Attach a .md, .txt or .csv file". Other formats are not read. Save the text in one of them. "The file does not look like UTF-8". Save it as UTF-8 and attach it again. "Larger than 100 000 bytes". Shorten the file or attach only the part the agent needs. "The file was cut". The model saw the first 20 000 characters; the plan itself is never truncated. "The plan is not ready yet". Wait for the plan ready status and open the plan from the task history. "The room changed". It changed while you were reading; ask the agent for a fresh plan. "Apply is blocked". The plan has a critical warning: a box outside the allowed coordinates (±1 000 000). Ask the agent for a fresh plan. TOO_MANY_OPERATIONS . The plan has more than 10 operations. It is not stored: split the task into parts. PLAN_TOO_LARGE . A plan above 300 objects or placements is refused by validation and not stored: there is no preview, and the task shows the failed status. Split the task. "The plan is already applied". It was applied in another tab. Nothing was written here; the objects are already in the room. If a simultaneous click in two tabs did double the objects, press ⌘Z and ask for a fresh plan. The task failed. A task cannot be resumed: read the reason in the history and set the task again. Only a card package can be resumed, with Resume in the Card jobs list.

en.title: Tidy up a selection
en.summary: Lay selected objects out in even columns: layouts, a before-and-after preview, one ⌘Z and the limits.
en.text: Result The selected objects stand in even columns, and free groups are covered by labelled block frames when the layout creates them. Sizes, texts and connectors stay as they are; one ⌘Z restores the previous positions and removes the created blocks. Who can Start it — an editor of the room and above. Agents are enabled in the organisation and in the room, and you have an active agent. Tidying is an agent task even when no model is called. An editor can open the preview and apply the plan : reading a plan requires edit permission in the room. A viewer has no Tidy up command: it is hidden. Before you start Select objects in the room: the set being laid out holds up to 50. The limit is counted after expansion: a selected group brings all its members, and a selected frame brings all its contents. Something in the selection must be able to move: the objects are free on the canvas or sit inside a selected frame. Locked objects and objects from unselected frames stay where they are. Kanban cards stay in place: their cell decides where they stand. When a card is in the selection, the plan still applies to the remaining objects, and the preview warns about the card. Steps Select the objects. Click Tidy up in the context menu or on the selection bar. Choose a layout. Auto is selected by default. Click Tidy up in the dialog. Result: the agent prepares a plan and the button reads "Preparing the layout…". Wait for the preview. Result: dashed lines in the room show where objects will move and which blocks will appear; the objects have not moved yet, and a task panel sits at the bottom. When needed, open Details and change the layout: the block labels are kept and the coordinates are recomputed. Click Apply . Result: the objects have moved, the block frames exist, and one ⌘Z puts everything back. Layouts Layout What it does Auto by prefixes when the texts carry them; otherwise by type By prefix one block per prefix; US-2 comes before US-10 By type one block per object type Grid an even grid with no block frames By meaning the model names blocks, the engine computes the coordinates A selected frame is laid out inside itself: its contents stand in columns, the frame itself does not move, and no nested frame appears. What goes to the model Only the selection text: object ids, types and texts, at most 50 objects and 20 000 characters. Coordinates, room titles, comments and people are not sent. The model may return block labels and a layout choice; the engine always computes the coordinates. Tidying works without a provider key: the layout is deterministic, and no warning about the model appears. A warning appears only when the model is configured and did not answer. Check the result The objects stand in even columns, and free groups are covered by labelled frames. Sizes, texts and connectors are unchanged. Locked objects and objects from unselected frames did not move. One ⌘Z restores the previous coordinates and removes the created blocks. Limitations Up to 50 objects in the set being laid out: the limit is counted after groups and frames are expanded. A larger selection is refused before a plan is stored. A kanban card stays in place: its cell decides where it stands. The plan applies to the rest of the selection. A frame is not stretched around its contents: if the objects do not fit, enlarge the frame or select fewer. Blocks are frames, never groups. An applied plan cannot be laid out again.

en.title: Apps in a room
en.summary: What apps are, how to open the panel, what “Hello” does, and why foreign code never runs here.
en.text: What it is An app adds a panel to the room. An app is described by a schema : the server sends a panel and the room draws it with its own components. No foreign code runs in the browser — no JavaScript, no HTML, no iframe. How to open it More ▾ → Apps in the room header. The panel lists the apps installed in the organisation that owns the room. A room without an organisation says so. “Hello” The app.hello app shows a Say hello button. Pressing it sends an action to the server; the server answers with a sentence carrying your name, and the panel shows it. Every press is audited as app.invoked and emitted to the organisation's events, so an integration can react to it. Who installs it An organisation administrator. The same admin can disable an app: it disappears from the panel entirely and its actions stop answering. The available apps are only the ones built into the product; an arbitrary schema or foreign code cannot be installed. What is not supported A marketplace, third-party apps, iframes and loading external code. If that ever arrives, it arrives as its own decision, not as a quiet setting.

en.title: Fill in card fields
en.summary: Status, assignee and a date range: what a card stores and how to change it.
en.text: Result A card keeps a status, one assignee and a date range. These fields appear on the card and are edited on the Properties panel; they do not replace the kanban column. Steps Select a card in the room, or click + in an empty kanban cell: the card is created in that column and swimlane and its text editor opens immediately. On the Properties panel, open Card fields. Choose a status: To do, In progress or Done. The empty value removes the status. Choose an assignee from the room's people, or leave it Unassigned. Set a start and a due date. Either can be empty; the card then shows one date. To clear a date, remove its value. Check the result The card shows its status, assignee name and dates. The values are the same after a reload. An overdue date is marked ! and by colour, not colour alone. The save indicator shows saved. Limits Status and column are independent: moving a card to another column does not change its status. One assignee; multiple assignees are not in v1. The assignee's email is not shown on the card. The picker lists people with access to the room; a link visitor is not included. Tags are a separate room vocabulary; add them to a card in the Tags block (up to 10 per object).

en.title: Discuss an object in comments
en.summary: A thread on an object or point: replies, resolve and reopen.
en.text: Result A discussion is anchored to an object or a point on the room. A thread survives object deletion, a reply reopens a resolved thread, and unread threads are visible in the panel. Steps Click the discussion icon in the header (it carries the unread count) or a pin on the canvas. Result: a panel with the thread list. Click New comment . If an object is selected, the thread is anchored to it; otherwise to the centre of the view. Enter the text and send it. Open a thread to read replies. Resolve closes it; a reply opens it again. The author may delete their own comment; a room manager may delete any. Check Threads, replies and pins are still there after a reload; a pin sits on the object or point. Deleting an object does not delete the thread: it is marked "object deleted". A commenter writes comments but cannot change the document. A link visitor does not see the discussion. Limits Comments work online; a reply draft is kept, sending waits for a connection and says so. One thread has one anchor, object or point; no nested threads. Mentions and notifications are not in v1. PNG/PDF can include open threads: numbered pins and a list below the room; resolved threads are not printed.

en.title: Create a connector between objects
en.summary: Join two sticky notes, shapes or other objects with a line and an arrow.
en.text: Result Two objects are joined by a line. When at least one end is a shape, the line has an arrow. Before you start You need edit permission on the room. A connector can join sticky notes, text, shapes, images, stickers and cards. A frame, a kanban and another connector cannot: they have no anchors. Steps Select an object. Four anchors appear around it, one at the middle of each side. Click an anchor. When the slot beside it is free, a connected copy of the object appears one gap away. When another connectable object stands there, the two are joined with a line. The second end lands on the nearest anchor. Or drag from the anchor to the second object and release on it. The result is the same: a line between the two objects. If you change your mind, press Esc or click an empty spot: no connector is made. Check the result A line is visible between the objects; on a selected connector the ends are hollow circles, and every sufficiently long segment has a filled middle. A pair that already had a line did not get a second one. ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z undoes the whole gesture: the line and the copy, when one appeared. If it did not work No anchors. The object cannot be connected: it is a frame, a kanban or another connector. A card connects through its cell. No connector was made. You may have landed on the same object: a self-connector is not allowed. Or the pair already has a line — a second one is not created. A copy appeared instead of a line. The slot was free; to join, point the anchor at an existing object or drag the line to it. No arrow is visible. An arrow appears when at least one end is a shape. A connector between sticky notes may have no arrow.

en.title: Connector keyboard reference
en.summary: Walk points, move and delete them without a mouse.
en.text: Result You can walk the points of a selected connector, move them and delete them without a mouse. Keys Action Keys Next point Tab Previous point Shift + Tab Move by 1 px arrow keys Move by 10 px Shift + arrow keys Delete a point Delete or Backspace Leave point navigation Esc How it works Select a connector with the mouse or keyboard. Press Tab ; the first rigid point gets a focus ring. Tab / Shift+Tab walk the points, arrows move the focused one. Delete removes it; Esc clears the focus and keeps the connector selected. Limits The walk covers rigid points. Connector ends and automatic midpoints are not included. A connector without rigid points does not start a walk on Tab . Ports and creating a new connector still use the mouse or trackpad.

en.title: Add a point and change a connector's route
en.summary: Place a rigid point, bend the line, switch between straight, elbow and curved.
en.text: Result The connector gets a point you placed yourself, or its shape changes. The ends stay attached to their objects. Steps Select the connector. Hollow ends, rigid points and filled segment midpoints appear. To add a point, drag a filled midpoint and release it where you want the point. To move a point, drag its hollow circle. To delete a point, double-click it. The two adjacent segments merge into one. To change the shape, open the connector bar and switch between straight, elbow and curved. Rigid points survive a routing change, moving the objects and reattaching an end. In curved mode they are supports: the line bends around them instead of passing through. Check the result Dragging a midpoint adds exactly one point and one undo entry. ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z restores the segment. After deleting a point the new segment has one midpoint instead of two. A connector has at most 32 points. Trying to add a 33rd shows a message and adds nothing. A segment shorter than 24 px has no midpoint, so handles do not overlap. If it did not work The point does not move. The connector is locked; unlock it. No midpoint appears. The segment is too short; move the objects apart. The curve is far from the point. It is a support, not a stop; that is intended.

en.title: Backup and restore
en.summary: An open JSON room backup with a checksum, and restore from a remo backup only.
en.text: Result You get a file that can restore the room, and you can restore a room from such a file. A backup always contains the whole room, regardless of the selection. What is inside manifest — format, version, date, object count and checksum. widgets — room objects: notes, cards, shapes, frames, connectors, kanbans. texts and textDeltas — text and formatting. kanbans — columns, swimlanes and card placements. groupNames , tags , presentation — group names, the tag vocabulary and presentation order. comments — threads and messages; author names are kept, the account link is not. assets — attachments; the list is empty in v1 because images are not stored in the document yet. It is plain JSON: you can read, verify and keep it without remo. Download a backup Open the room menu (the room’s name) and choose Export…. Choose the Room backup format. Click Export. The downloaded filename comes from the room title and preserves Cyrillic letters, for example план-ёж.remo-backup.json . You need the board.backup grant; editors, co-owners and owners have it. Every download is recorded in the audit log. Restore a room Open the room menu → Restore from backup…: the dialog opens on the restore section, with the file picker. Choose a file. remo checks the format, version and checksum. Check the file name and object count, then confirm the replacement. Import replaces the whole room content, not adds objects, and replaces the discussion: an empty comment list clears the threads. An object lock is restored with the object. The action cannot be undone for everyone, so back up the current room first. Check The file opens as JSON, with manifest and a checksum. After import the object count matches the dialog and the room opens for every participant. Comments and tags are visible in the same places after import. If it did not work "This is not a remo room backup". The file was made by another program, or it is not JSON. "The checksum does not match". The file is damaged or was edited; use the original backup. "Made by a newer remo version". Update remo or use a backup in a supported version. No restore section. You need both board.edit and board.backup .

en.title: PNG and PDF
en.summary: A picture for a chat and a one-page PDF: which to choose and who may export.
en.text: Result You get a file with the chosen scope: a PNG for a chat or a document, or a one-page PDF with the same picture. Formats PNG — lossless, no transparency is needed, the background comes from the theme. Good for chat, slides and documents. PDF — the same picture on one page. Proportions are kept; text in the PDF is not editable or searchable. Room backup — a separate format for moving data, not a picture. See the Backup and restore topic. A backup keeps the table layout and each object's cell. A section table in PNG/PDF is drawn with its grid, headers and fills: it is part of the section, not screen chrome. Who may export PNG and PDF — the board.export grant. Viewers, commenters, editors and owners have it. Backup — the board.backup grant. Editors, co-owners and owners have it. Backup import — the board.manage grant. Co-owners and owners have it. A public-link visitor gets neither a picture nor a backup: a link is a view grant, not a data-egress grant. Steps Open the room menu (the room’s name) and choose Export…. Choose a scope and a format. Click Export and wait for "The file is ready". If it did not work No Export entry in the room menu. You have neither board.export nor board.backup ; ask the owner for access. A format is unavailable. Your role does not have the matching grant. The export failed. The room was not changed. Retry: the request is kept, and a retry does not create a second request.

en.title: What an export includes
en.summary: Export scope: selection, frame or the whole room. The dialog shows the object count and never picks the whole room silently.
en.text: Result The file contains exactly the chosen scope — the selected objects, one frame with its contents, or the whole room — together with the connectors inside it. The dialog shows the object count. Scopes Selection — the objects selected right now, and the connectors between them. If a frame or a kanban is selected, its child objects are included too. Frame — the frame that contains the selected object, with everything inside it. If no frame is selected and the selection is not inside one, the option is unavailable. Whole room — every object. This option is chosen explicitly; the dialog never substitutes it for a selection. Connectors in the scope A connector is a relation between two objects, not a third object, so it goes into the file together with both of its ends. A marquee drawn around two objects selects the connector between them too. A connector whose other end is outside the scope is left out of the file: a line cut at the edge would claim a relation to an object the picture does not show. A connector between two cards of the same kanban counts as internal when the kanban is in the scope. A connector selected on its own is exported as before — clipped at the picture edge. Steps Open the room menu (the room’s name) and choose Export…. Choose a scope. The object count is shown under the options. Choose a format and click Export. Check the result The picture has no grid, selection outlines or other people's cursors: those are screen chrome, not the room. The object count in the dialog, connectors included, matches what the file shows. Choosing Selection with nothing selected leaves the export button disabled. Limits A very large room is exported at a lower resolution but in full: the limit protects the browser from running out of memory.

en.title: Follow a participant
en.summary: A mirrored view and zoom, a public counter, stopping from either side, and a bring-everyone invitation.
en.text: Result You see the same part of the room at the same zoom as the chosen person. Others can follow you the same way, and you can stop that. Steps Click a participant's avatar in the header. Your view moves to theirs; a pill appears: "Following …". Click Stop on the pill to leave. Public counter Next to the avatars, the eye icon with a number shows how many people are following you right now. Click the counter to open the list, stop everyone, or bring everyone to you. Pause If you pan or zoom yourself, following pauses: the pill says "Following paused" and offers Resume. The view never snaps back. Stopping from either side The follower clicks Stop. The followed person clicks "Stop everyone": the followers' pills disappear with a message that the follow was stopped. Bring everyone to me "Bring everyone to me" is an invitation, not a jump: each person gets "Follow / Stay". If the group agreed in advance, an editor can turn on "Follow automatically", and the invitation moves viewports without a prompt. Limits Following is not saved: closing the tab ends it, and it never appears in a backup or an export. A public-link visitor sees no participants and cannot follow. The counter is public; hiding the fact of following from the followed person is not allowed.

en.title: Shared timer
en.summary: One countdown for the whole room: start, pause, +1 minute and time is up, the same for everyone.
en.text: Result One shared timer appears in the room. Everybody sees the same remaining time and who set it. A late joiner sees the current countdown, and reloading the page does not reset it. Who may control it An editor or above controls the timer — the board.facilitate grant. A viewer or commenter sees the countdown but no controls. Steps Open Facilitation ▾ and choose Timer. Pick 1, 5, 10 or 15 minutes, or type your own. Click Start. The timer appears in the middle of the current view and becomes selected. While it runs, the Timer row in Facilitation ▾ shows the time left. Open the menu and click Timer to open the controls. Controls Pause keeps the exact remaining time and names who paused it. Resume continues from the same value. +1 min adds a minute; after "time is up" it starts a fresh one-minute countdown. Reset returns the timer to "not started" and keeps the chosen length. Check the result Open the room in a second tab: the countdown matches to the second. Pause: both tabs show one value and one name. Let it reach zero: the timer says "Time is up" and stays in the room until reset. Limits The timer is a room object: it travels into a backup and an export as a card with a time. There is no personal stopwatch in this version: the countdown in the room is always shared.

en.title: Voting on objects
en.summary: A session with a quota per person, an anonymous tally and results on the room.
en.text: Result Participants spread a limited number of votes across the chosen objects right in the room. The server counts votes and the quota, so reloading the page or opening a second tab does not give anyone extra votes. Voting stops by itself when the time is up — there is no voting "after the bell". Who may Start a session — an editor or above ( board.facilitate ). Vote — everyone who can see the room, including a public-link visitor. A visitor has a quota per browser and is never asked for a name. End for all, extend and publish — an editor only. Steps Start the shared timer if the vote should follow a common clock: it then ends with the timer. Select the objects to vote on. Open Facilitation ▾ and choose Voting. On the New session tab set the votes per person, the duration and anonymity. When the room timer runs, the "With the timer" option is available and shows the time left. Click Start voting. How to vote You vote on the object: a counter with "+" appears in its bottom-right corner. A line above the room — "Voting is on" — shows the votes you have left, the time and who leads the session; the same line opens the panel. "+" casts a vote. When you have already voted for the object, the counter is highlighted, labelled "yours" and shows "−" to take the vote back. The number is always the sum for the object, not your share. When no votes are left, "+" is off and explains why. Voting happens in the room only: the panel has no voting buttons. Counters update for everyone at once; there is no need to move the room. What you see On the Manage tab, three numbers: time left, how many people voted and how many votes were cast. The session's objects with bars and totals; "Show in the room" selects an object and brings the camera to it. Totals per object — no names when the session is anonymous. With an anonymous session only totals are visible: nobody sees who voted for what, including the facilitator. Ending and results Voting closes by time automatically; End now… closes it earlier and asks for confirmation first. After it closes the voting buttons disappear, each object keeps its number marked "total", and the server refuses new votes. The Results tab names the leader, lists the places with bars for each share and states ties in words ("Places 2–3 shared by …"). In an open session the results name people: an object's row opens with a button and shows who gave it votes, and the "Summary" block shows how much each person spent and across how many objects. Guests via the link are counted, not named. The "What participants will see" block shows the card that will appear in the room. Publish in the room writes it as a separate text object: a title, places and votes (up to 10), and the number of participants. It is ordinary text without formatting: lines like "1. … — N", with no bold or headings. Previous sessions stay under Previous sessions on the Results tab. An unpublished session can be published from there. If it did not work "No votes left". You used every vote; take one back with "−" on the object. "Session closed". The time is up or the facilitator ended it. "A session is already open". End the current one first. An object has no counter. It was not in the session's snapshot: objects added later do not take part.

en.title: Lock an object from edits
en.summary: An author lock: who may release it and what copies do.
en.text: Result A locked object cannot be resized, edited or deleted, but it can still be selected and moved. The lock records its author: only the author or a room manager can release it. Steps Select the object and click Lock in the menu or press ⌘⇧L / Ctrl+Shift+L . To release it, select the object and click Unlock . If somebody else locked it, the interface names them and points you to the author or a room manager. Unlock everything you can in the menu releases your locks; a room manager releases every lock. Check A second editor can move the object but cannot resize, edit or delete it. The author releases their lock; a room manager releases somebody else's. A copy or duplicate of a locked object appears unlocked. The object's info shows who locked it. Limits A lock is coordination, not access control: it stops accidental edits in the interface, not a direct document write. An old lock with no recorded author can be released by any editor, until it is toggled once. A lock on a frame does not lock its contents; to protect a group, select it and lock the members.

en.title: Object name and ID
en.summary: An object label for search and presentation; a stable ID and copying.
en.text: Result An object has an optional Name for search and presentation and a permanent ID for links and commands. The name is not painted on the canvas; the ID never changes. Steps Select an object in the room. In the inspector, fill in Name and press Enter or click outside the field. An empty value removes the name. The ID beside it is read-only. Click Copy ID to paste it into a link, a command or a bug report. Check The name appears in the presentation object list and is found by search. The name did not appear on the canvas and did not change the object's text. The ID stayed the same after renaming and reloading. Limits A name does not have to be unique: two objects may share one. An ID cannot be changed; it is the object's stable identity. An empty name means "no name"; the presentation label falls back to the title, text or ID.

en.title: Organisation and teams
en.summary: Personal and shared organisation, renaming, teams and their members.
en.text: Result You know how a personal organisation differs from a shared one, can rename the organisation, and run teams: create, rename, delete and add members. Personal and shared Personal — the organisation every account has. Work alone or with an interest group; the Personal badge marks it in the list. Shared — an additional organisation for work, a club or a client. Create it with + New organisation under Organisation and people . Permissions and rooms work the same way; the kind only changes the badge and the fact that the personal organisation always stays with the account. Steps Open the account menu → Organisation and people . To rename the organisation, click Rename , enter the name and save. An organisation administrator can do this. In the Teams block, create a team: enter a name and click + Create team . In a team row, rename or delete it. A team can be deleted only when no room or grant refers to it; otherwise the product shows the room and grant counts. Expand the team members, add a person from the organisation and choose a role: team admin or member. Remove a member in the same place. Check The screen title shows the new organisation name. The renamed team appears in the list and in the team picker when creating a room. The deleted team is gone; rooms that referred to it were not allowed to be deleted. A newly added member appears in the team list. Limits Renaming the organisation and managing teams belongs to the organisation administrator. A personal organisation cannot be deleted: it stays with the account. A guest sees only their own seat and not the organisation's people directory.

en.title: Present the room
en.summary: Slide order from any objects, presenter and followers, return to the presenter and stop.
en.text: Result Show the room one slide at a time. You can use a frame or another object as a slide and choose the order. Participants see the current slide. When you stop presenting, your previous view returns. Before you start The room has objects. A slide can be a frame, a sticky note, a card, a shape or another object. You are a facilitator (editor, co-owner or owner). The frame's size is the slide's size: if a section needs more room, resize the frame by a corner before presenting; a table section takes its size from its columns and rows. The contents are not scaled. For other objects the camera fits their rectangle, and for a connector it fits both ends. When a section is shown as a table , it steps through cells: top to bottom by rows and left to right inside a row. Empty cells are skipped; a table with no objects is one whole slide. The camera shows the cell with its headers, and the bottom bar names the column and row. Followers follow the same cell. Steps Click the ▶ icon (Start presentation) in the header. Result: a panel with the slides and an object list. Add an object with Add or Add selection , and find it by name, title or text. Reorder slides with the arrows; Add all frames adds the remaining frames. A slide label comes from the object name, then its title or text; a short id sits beside it to tell same-named objects apart. Name objects in advance in the inspector: select an object and fill in Name . The name is not painted on the canvas, does not have to be unique, and the ID beside it is read-only. Click Start presentation in the panel. Result: the first slide appears with a counter. Move with ‹ and › or the PageDown and PageUp keys: the arrow keys pan the canvas, not the slides. Participants see "{name} is showing the room" and click Watch ; they join the current slide. Stop closes the mode. The presenter returns to the previous view; followers stay on the last slide. Check A late participant starts at the current slide, not the first one. "Return to presenter" goes back to the current slide after panning away. After stopping, the presenter sees the same view as before the start. With no slides, the panel explains what to add. Limits Any object can be a slide; there is no separate "slide" object type. Object names are not unique: two objects may share a name, and the id remains their identity. One presenter; followers cannot advance. If a presentation is already running, a second one cannot start: the product names the presenter and offers Watch. The presentation is not recorded and does not enter room history. A link visitor may watch but cannot start a presentation.

en.title: Palette
en.summary: One palette for the rail and the object bar: seven tones, white, black and transparent, keys 1–7.
en.text: Result An object has several roles: sheet or fill, border, text, line and connector label. Each takes its value from one palette — seven tones at three levels plus white, black and transparent. A colour is changed on the object bar, in the rail or with keys 1–7, and has the same name everywhere. The grid Seven tones run in columns: grey, yellow, orange, pink, violet, blue, green. Levels 100 and 300 are fills; 600 is for lines, borders and text. Tone 100 300 600 Grey Grey Dark grey Graphite Yellow Yellow Ochre Deep ochre Orange Orange Taupe Terracotta Pink Pink Dusty pink Deep raspberry Violet Violet Lilac Deep violet Blue Blue Grey blue Deep blue Green Green Sage Deep green Named colours White and Black stand in a separate column to the left of the grid. A shape's Fill also offers Transparent , and a Border or a Line offers None : both are the same stored value, but a role without a fill and a role without a line are named differently. Transparent is drawn as a checkerboard. A sticky note has no transparency: its sheet is the object. Where to change a colour A new sticky note. The caret beside the Sticky note tool in the rail opens the palette: 14 fills plus White and Black. Yellow is marked as the default. A sticky note. Click the sample on the object bar to open Sheet colour and Text . A shape. The sample opens presets, Fill , Border and Text . Text. On a sticky note or a shape the Text role offers Auto, Dark, Black, White ; on free text it offers Auto, Black, White . A connector. The sample opens Line , and when the connector has text, also Text (the connector label): Auto, Black, White . Several objects. On the selection bar the sample shows the shared fill or line. Mixed colours means the objects disagree. Keys 1–7 A digit picks a tone and paints the main role of the selection: sticky notes and shapes get a fill; the 100 or 300 row is kept, and different rows fall back to 100; a connector gets its line, always 600; text gets its colour, always 600. A key works when only objects with that role are selected. In an input field, a menu or a dialog, a digit stays a digit. Named colours have no number. Custom colour A value outside the palette is labelled Custom colour below the grid. That is a label for the value, not a swatch to pick: only palette values can be chosen. The current value is kept until you choose another: the room is not repainted after the fact. Sticky notes from the previous palette The 100 and 300 fills are now paper tones: muted, with dark text readable on every one. A sticky note painted earlier stays bright. The window names its colour by tone and level, for example Yellow , and marks that swatch. Click the swatch or press the digit and the note takes the new paper tone. An administrator can repaint every room at once with pnpm db:repaint . Check the result The rail and the sticky note window show the same 14 fills in the same order, with White and Black in a separate column. The name on the sample matches the name of the chosen swatch in the window. After pressing 4, a sticky note becomes pink on its previous level. An object with Custom colour stays that way until you pick a colour from the palette. Limitations Colour does not affect access rights. A sticky note has no transparency; free text and a connector label have the Auto / Black / White control, while sticky note and shape text has Auto / Dark / Black / White. The palette does not change an object's type, layer or size.

en.title: Create a room
en.summary: A new room in an organisation (and a team when one is chosen).
en.text: Result A new room is created in your organisation — in a team when one is chosen — and opened. It is either empty or contains the chosen template; the name can be changed in the header. Steps Open All rooms in the header. If you belong to several organisations, choose one in the Organisation field — the previous room closes and the list shows the new organisation's rooms. Enter a name. If there are several organisations or teams, choose the right ones. Create an organisation in the account menu under Organisation and people with + New organisation ; create a team in the Teams block (organisation admin). Choose Empty room or a template. The template arrives in the account language: Russian copy for a Russian profile, English copy for an English one. Click Create. Check the result The new room opens and its id is in the address. The name matches the one you entered. A room created from a template opens with the template’s objects. An empty room opens with a blank canvas. Limits A guest cannot create a room: the button is disabled and a direct request is refused. Ask the organisation administrator. Creation belongs to an active organisation member. A view-only link does not grant it. A template can be added later from More ▾ → Templates… .

en.title: Organisation home
en.summary: Room tiles, search, sorting, pages, emoji and switching organisation.
en.text: Result You see the organisation home: room tiles with an emoji, title, team, author and dates. The same screen carries name search, sorting, pages and the organisation switcher. Before you start You are signed in. Every account has a personal organisation with the Personal badge; it is fine for working alone or with an interest group. From a room, click All rooms in the header or the organisation name left of the room title. Steps Open All rooms . Result: the address is ?org=… , the room is closed, and the chosen organisation's tiles are shown. Choose an organisation in the Organisation field. Result: the previous room and organisation are left behind and the list shows the new organisation's rooms. Search by room name. Result: the list narrows; an empty answer says nothing matches. Choose a sort: Updated , Created , Name or Author . The arrow beside it changes direction. Result: tiles flow left to right, then top to bottom, in that order. Page through 24 tiles at a time with the numbers and ‹ › arrows. Click a tile to open the room. The tile menu changes the emoji, duplicates or trashes the room when you have the right. Click New room to create one in the chosen organisation. Trash beside Rooms shows deleted rooms; Restore puts a room back in the list. Only the owner can restore. Check The header names the organisation and shows the Personal badge for a personal one. A tile carries the title, team, author Name @handle , creation date and update date. The emoji survives a reload. A deleted room appears in the trash and restores back to the list. After switching organisation the previously open room is no longer shown. Limits The room icon is one emoji. Images and uploaded icons come later. The author is the creator; handing over ownership does not rewrite history. For older rooms the creation date was restored from the last update and may be approximate. Search looks at the room name, not the text on the canvas.

en.title: Show a section as a table
en.summary: A section's title and view, cells, merge, sizes, appearance and safe deletions.
en.text: Result A section (frame) can be shown as a table: it gets columns and rows, and objects stay in cells. The free view and the table are two views of one section; text, links, comments and the objects themselves are neither copied nor lost. Title and view The section's title sits above its top-left corner. Double-click the title, or press F2 or Enter , to edit it: Enter or leaving the field commits, Esc cancels, and one ⌘Z undoes it. The title is the section's label, not an object: it is outside the table rectangle and never gets in the way of moving objects. In table mode a Table badge appears after the title. Click it to open the Section / Table menu; there is no badge in the free view. The same switch is in Properties and in the section's context menu. Switching keeps the objects and the camera; Remove table in the panel asks for confirmation, while the badge switches at once and says the cells are kept. Steps Select the section and open Properties . A section just created with Gather into section opens the panel for you. Choose Table . If the section already holds objects, the How to lay out the material? question opens: lay it out by its current position or keep everything in the first cell. The canvas shows a preview; Apply is one undo step. + Column and + Row add axes. Choose an axis in the panel or by clicking its header on the canvas; clicking the header again opens its menu: rename, insert a neighbour, move, turn, size, delete. A double click on a header (or Enter / F2 ) edits the title in place: Enter commits, Tab moves to the next header, Esc cancels. Click an empty part of a cell: the first click selects the section, the second selects the cell. Shift+click another cell selects a rectangular range; the arrow keys move the cell, Shift+arrows extend the range, Esc clears it. Merge appears above the range; a merged cell offers Split . The same actions live in the cell menu (right click or Shift+F10 ), together with inserting and duplicating rows and columns. Drag an object or a selection to another cell: it lands there keeping its relative arrangement. A header does not take objects. The same move is available as Move to cell… in the selected object's properties. If an axis holds objects, deleting it asks first: move them to the neighbouring axis (the default) or delete them with the axis. Remove table returns the free view; cells are remembered, and turning the table on again restores the structure. Delete section removes only the frame: the objects stay on the canvas. Sizes Each axis has two modes. Auto follows the content both ways. Manual remembers the visible size: content may grow the axis, but the axis never shrinks on its own. Drag a header boundary to switch to Manual ; a double click on the boundary or Delete returns to Auto . The Narrow / Medium / Wide presets are manual sizes. For a merged cell the panel switch applies to every column and row of the block; a mixed state is shown separately. Appearance The Table appearance group holds fills, Borders and Cell padding . The area is chosen in the window: table, headers, the selected axis or the selected cell. A border has a colour, width and style (solid, dashed, no border); padding is small, medium, large or a number. As before restores the default. A border is drawn around the whole cell; padding changes how much room the content takes, and the cell grows around it. Long titles Column and row titles wrap by words; the header grows for a vertical or multi-line title and the row strip grows for a long name. Text longer than 100 characters is shortened with an ellipsis. Text is never squeezed or distorted. Keyboard and screen reader Tab moves through the section title, the view badge and the table headers; Enter or F2 edits a title, Enter commits, Esc cancels. In the table the arrow keys move the selected cell, Shift+arrows extend the range, and Shift+F10 opens the cell menu. A screen reader reads the section as a table: columns, rows and cell contents; the selected axis and the selected cell are announced separately. Move to cell… also works from the keyboard. Check After any action and after "Remove table" → "Table" the texts, links and positions are intact. Merge and split undo with one ⌘Z; objects from covered cells stay in the top-left cell. A move into a cell keeps the objects' relative arrangement and undoes with one ⌘Z. With auto size off an axis does not shrink after an object is removed; with it on the axis follows the content again. "Remove table" does not delete objects; the confirmation names how many objects stay. One ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z undoes the whole action. Limits A table is a view of a section, not a separate object; kanban stays a different tool. A border applies to the whole cell; there are no per-side borders. A table does not change access: the room is still the unit of access.

en.title: Save status and offline
en.summary: Saved, saving or offline: what the topbar indicator means and what happens to edits without a connection.
en.text: Result The header shows one of three states: Saved , Saving or Offline (N) . Saved — the server confirmed that the edits are stored. It does not mean "stored in the browser": confirmation arrives over the socket after the server persists them. Saving — an edit was sent but is not acknowledged yet. This is usually under a second. Offline (N) — there is no connection; N edits are waiting. They stay in this tab and are sent after reconnect. Offline If the connection drops, keep working: edits stay in the document. When the connection returns, the status changes to Saving , then Saved . Wait for saved before closing the tab. If too many edits accumulate, input stops: the indicator shows Offline · input paused , and a message appears above the room. This protects the queue from growing without bound. Reconnect and wait for Saved to continue. Too many edits The server limits the write rate. If there are too many edits in a short time, it closes the connection and shows the reason. What you entered stays in the current tab: closing the connection cancels neither text nor inserted objects. A message about changes coming too fast appears above the room. Stop the bulk action: a paste, a bulk move, or a change to many objects at once. Wait for reconnect. Before retrying, the client waits 5 seconds and doubles the pause up to 60 seconds. Continue once the status changes to Saving , then Saved . The room is full The room has a size limit. When it is reached, the server accepts only small changes: typing, moving and deleting go through, a large paste does not. The connection closes because the room reached its size limit; the paste stays in this tab and is not saved. Delete unneeded objects or large fragments from the room. Wait for reconnect: the pause before retry starts at 30 seconds and doubles up to 5 minutes. Paste again in smaller parts. Too many objects A separate limit is the object count: 20,000 per room. When it is reached, the server does not accept new objects, but existing ones can be changed, moved and deleted. This is not the size limit: a room can take little space and still hit the object count. The connection closes as it does for a full room, but the cause is different. Delete unneeded objects to reduce the count. Wait for reconnect: the pause before retry is 30 seconds to 5 minutes. Add new objects after the count drops below the limit. If access was revoked If the owner changes your role while you work, the server closes the connection. The room stays on screen but becomes read-only, with an "Access changed" message. Save what you need before the change or ask for access again. What to check The indicator in the header next to the help button. After an edit it shows Saving , then Saved . Offline, the N counter grows with each edit. After a page reload, saved edits are still there. After a speed or limit close, the connection returns by itself; the status changes to Saving , then Saved . In a full room a small edit saves, while a large paste does not. After deleting extra content, new objects can be added again. Limits Offline edits and edits waiting for reconnect live in the current tab. If the tab is closed before saving, unsent work is lost. The queue limit protects against unbounded growth; it is not a promise of unlimited offline work. The size limit and the object limit are set by the server. They do not delete data: the room stays readable and can be cleaned up.

en.title: Tag objects and link them
en.summary: A room tag vocabulary and a link on an object: an external address or another object.
en.text: Result Tags group objects by meaning, and a link on an object leads to a source or to another room object. Both survive a reload and are included in a backup. Tags Select a card or a sticky note. On the Properties panel's Tags block, enter a name, choose a colour and click Add. Tick the tag under "Tags on this object". Result: the object carries the tag. Click "Select (N)" on a tag. Result: the objects with that tag are selected; nothing is hidden, so the change is visible. Rename the tag in its row or delete it. A rename changes the label everywhere; a delete removes it from every object. Links Select one object. In the Link block, paste an external https://… address and click Apply. Or choose a room object in the list and click its Apply. Click Open to follow the link, or Remove to clear it. Check Tags and the link are still there after a reload. Renaming a tag does not create a second tag. An external link opens in a new window; an internal one opens the object on this room. A javascript: or data: link is refused. Limits One tag is one room record; 50 tags per room and 10 per object. A link grants no access: opening an internal link still checks rights. An external link is not embedded or fetched by the server; it only opens. An internal link can only target an object on this room.
